findings.summary: U1 (the ⭐ reachability criterion and the central thesis of this package: runGenerate has zero callers) has NO behavioral test. The spec explicitly requires a positive/negative pair driven from the production entry (tick-entry --run / runChannelWrite) and explicitly forbids 'asserting the function exists or the decision is true counts' (断言「函数存在」或「决策为真」不算数). The only U1 case that touches the production path (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:62-72) reads src/tick-run.ts as a STRING and asserts expect(source).toContain('runGenerate') — exactly the forbidden 'function exists' shape. The other two U1 cases are pure decideGenerate unit tests, also explicitly disqualified. The G4b sibling package demonstrates the correct pattern at test/g4b-termination-wiring.test.ts:161-176 (drive runChannelWrite with a stubbed converged board, assert outcome.termination), so this is a missing test, not a framework limit.

Mutation T1 ('remove the production call to runGenerate, reverting to the pre-change state') is NOT killed by any test. Removing the 'await runGenerate(generateDeps, cfg)' call at src/tick-run.ts:1495 leaves every U1 case green: the source-grep still matches the import/comment text, and no test asserts runGenerate is actually invoked at runtime from runChannelWrite. The spec's gate language is explicit: '⛔ 杀不掉即判 U1 零功率' (if T1 cannot be killed, U1 is judged zero-power). The dev-note even confesses T1 is 'verified' by source-level grep, which is a text search, not a mutation kill. Required fix: a behavioral runChannelWrite test that injects fake generateDeps (spawnRole/writeDoc/spawnExport spies) and asserts (a) on a converged board + --origin, outcome.generateTriggered === true AND the spies were called; (b) on termination.state === null, outcome.generateTriggered === false AND the spies were never called. That pair would kill T1.

U2 (one-shot: same origin observed by two consecutive ticks must trigger generate exactly once) is likewise verified only by source-string grep (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:88-110 asserts source contains 'generatedOrigins.has(origin)' and that add() precedes generateTriggered=true by string indexOf). This has no runtime power: mutation T2 ('drop the one-shot guard so every tick runs generate') would not be killed, because no test drives runChannelWrite twice against the same origin and asserts writeDoc/spawn counts stayed at 1. Required fix: call runChannelWrite twice with the same --origin and a converged board, assert the second outcome.generateTriggered === false and that injected writeDoc/spawnExport were called exactly once total.

The dev-note (docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_g4c_generate_wiring_01.md:3) records input_commit as 6356dfd3bbf7896ccce917d0e49bd0a4061295d2, which is neither the dispatch input_commit (bce88d3...) nor the target_base_commit (f655317...). The spec's delivery note (approved.md:136-138) clarifies the field's real meaning is the implement attempt's input_commit and forbids making extra commits just to align the hash, so this is a record-keeping note only — not a product defect — but the recorded value appears stale relative to this attempt.
